report.summary: The release improves drawing editing and recovery while changing compatibility with some imported data.
keyChanges: The four one-step and all-the-way layer-change operations now return the modified element list; previously, the editor assigned their missing return value instead of retaining the drawing, so verify each operation keeps the drawing available and applies the requested order.

Undo and redo now return the restored drawing for the editor to apply, and invalid history data returns no replacement instead of throwing; valid history snapshots retain their previous behavior. The drawing and rendering inputs are also marked read-only, with no runtime behavior change.
Deleting selected elements now applies the filtered drawing list; previously the deletion result was discarded, so selected elements remained in the drawing.
On startup, saved drawing elements are restored separately from saved application state, with a refresh when no application state is available.
Keyboard movement, selection clearing, and style pasting now replace the scene array; undo and redo also adopt a returned scene when one is available.
Pasting text styles still recalculates text dimensions, while the enclosing style-paste action now triggers the refresh.

Removing selected objects now produces a new list containing only unselected objects instead of mutating the supplied list and returning no list; the editor uses that result for deletion and cut, so verify both actions leave the unselected drawing intact.

Scene creation still produces an empty drawing, while JSON export, local saving, and scrollbar calculations and hit detection now accept read-only element collections at the type level; their runtime behavior is unchanged.

Pasting now offsets each copied element by its original coordinates instead of subtracting the group’s minimum x and y, so drawings whose elements do not start at coordinate zero may appear in a different position.

Selected-element property changes now replace element records while retaining their other attributes; verify edits to colors, opacity, fill, stroke width, roughness, and text settings remain visible and preserve the rest of each element.
With Shift held, clicking empty canvas now retains the current selection; without Shift, empty-canvas clicks still clear it.
Scene loading now uses the elements returned by the load operation as the current drawing.
When saved view settings are malformed, startup now keeps valid drawing elements instead of clearing the drawing; verify recovery and continued use of those elements.
JSON import now treats malformed JSON as an empty drawing, but no longer converts a JSON-encoded string in the elements field into an element list, so a format accepted before may fail to load.
Selection lookup, text-placement lookup, and selected-element checks accept read-only collections; the changes affect the accepted input type, not runtime behavior.
Changing a selected element’s stroke color now preserves the element and its other properties instead of replacing it with the chosen color value, so the drawing remains editable after the change.
qaChecks: Verify the existing one-step earlier and later actions separately: the drawing remains available, and the selected shape moves exactly one position in the stacking order each time.
Check the existing all-the-way earlier and later actions separately: the drawing remains available, and the selected shape moves to the beginning or end of the stacking order as requested.
Verify that undoing or redoing an invalid history snapshot leaves the current drawing unchanged without an error.
Verify pressing Delete or Backspace with the selected element present removes it from the drawing while leaving the unselected element visible.
Verify startup with saved drawing elements but no saved application state; confirm the saved drawing appears in the editor.
Check undo and redo after making an edit; confirm undo restores the prior scene and redo restores the edited scene.
Test an arrow key with an element selected; confirm the element moves, then press Escape and confirm the selection clears.
Confirm pasting copied text styling onto a selected text object updates its appearance and text bounds in the editor.

Verify pasting a copied drawing whose elements have source x coordinates 100 and 200 and y coordinates 50 and 150 places the pasted elements with those original offsets retained, rather than resetting the group’s minimum coordinates to the paste position.

Check that after selecting multiple elements, changing their color, opacity, fill, stroke width, roughness, or text settings updates the selected elements while leaving their other visible properties intact.
Confirm that with an element selected, Shift-clicking empty canvas keeps the selection, while clicking empty canvas without Shift clears it.
Test loading a saved drawing while another drawing is already open; confirm the loaded drawing becomes the current drawing.
Verify selected-element deletion with one selected object and one unselected object removes the selected object while leaving the unselected object visible.
Check cutting the selected object removes it from the drawing while leaving the unselected object visible.
Confirm a drawing still opens with an empty scene and that normal editing, saving, JSON export, and scrollbar interaction behave as before.
Verify that opening the editor with valid saved drawing elements but malformed saved view settings still restores the drawing, and that its elements remain usable.
Check that importing a malformed .json file resolves to an empty drawing without stopping the editor.
Test importing a .json file with elements set to a JSON-encoded string containing an element array; confirm the drawing imports, as it did before this change.
Verify selecting the rectangle still displays the existing Background Color and Fill controls.
Verify that selecting one element and applying a different available stroke color updates its color while the element remains visible and selected.
uncertainty: The supplied context provides no way to create an invalid history snapshot or navigate to drawing history, so the specific changed error-handling case cannot be reproduced through a documented user flow; no ordinary user input is shown to behave differently before and after the change.
The layer-order updates now assign a reordered copy of the elements list, but the supplied evidence establishes no input where the resulting visible order differs from before.

The supplied evidence does not establish whether saved drawing elements without saved application state were rendered before this change; verify that restore case against expected persistence behavior.
No input was found that the old code handled differently from the new code; the supplied changes alter types rather than runtime behavior.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether loading a saved drawing is intended to replace the current drawing or combine with it; confirm the expected outcome for the final check.
The new import path passes a string-valued elements field to array processing, so the previously accepted JSON-encoded-string format may fail; confirm whether that format remains supported.
The changes affect an input type rather than runtime behavior, so a manual editor check cannot directly verify acceptance of read-only collections.

report.summary: The release expands drawing statistics and refines how selected objects and display settings behave in the editor.
keyChanges: Storage sizes in statistics are now shown with compact units: bytes use “b”, thousands “k”, millions “M”, and billions “G”, with trailing zero decimals removed.
Scene-storage size is calculated separately, but the overall storage total keeps the same inputs and counting rule as before.
Pending delayed work can now be canceled, but no supplied application usage shows this capability being invoked.
Statistics display is off by default, is retained when the canvas is cleared, is kept in browser storage, and is excluded from exported state.
Edge-sharpness changes now resolve the target elements as a set when deciding whether to update the defaults for newly drawn linear or non-linear elements.

The canvas context menu can open the Stats panel, which shows scene element count and rounded dimensions, storage sizes, and—when elements are selected—their position and dimensions; one selected element also shows its angle.
Storage-size readings are collected after a 500 ms debounce, so allow for a brief delay before checking them.
Selected-object editing controls now use the plural selection lookup to identify drawing objects; whether this changes which options appear is not established by the supplied diff.
A boolean state field for statistics visibility was added, but no changed runtime behavior or affected application area is evidenced.

Verify that clearing the canvas while statistics display is enabled leaves statistics display enabled.
Confirm that an enabled statistics-display preference remains enabled after reloading the editor.
Check that applying an edge-sharpness value to the mixed selection updates the selected elements, without changing either default sharpness for newly drawn elements.
Verify that opening the panel from the canvas context menu displays scene statistics and that closing the panel hides it.
Check a drawing with exactly two elements and nothing selected: the panel shows an element count of 2, rounded scene width and height, and scene and total storage sizes after the 500 ms update delay.

Verify the mixed selection still exposes editing options applicable to its selected objects.

The old and new storage-total calculations handle inputs identically, and the new cancellation capability has no supplied user-facing caller; no distinct regression input or route to verify was identified.

report.summary: The release updates the embedded editor’s integration and reusable-library workflows, with clearer access to editor actions and pointer position.
keyChanges: A library-import link is read from the URL hash, with a legacy query-parameter fallback; imported items are merged as published items, the library collection opens, and the import parameter is removed or the prior URL restored.
Library links are now detected by a dedicated handler, including legacy query-string links; matching links skip normal scene initialization and are handled as library imports.
Saved library items are initialized and refreshed separately from scene data, so QA should confirm they remain available after loading and after another browser tab updates them.

The supplied changes remove the library-file import helper and the routine that restored imported items and merged unique items with the existing Library; whether another path replaces them is unclear.
Importing a Library file now merges its items with the existing Library and opens the Library, while startup-provided items also merge with existing items.
The embedded editor now offers a dedicated Library-update capability in place of its previous URL-import capability; updates replace existing items by default unless merging is requested.
A Library link in the URL no longer automatically adds items when the editor starts, whether the link is in the URL fragment or the legacy query string.
Scene updates no longer apply Library items included with the scene data.
Loading a valid drawing file updates the Scene, while loading a valid Library file now imports its items and opens the Library instead of treating the file contents as a Scene.
The example now uses the editor API to add its initial image and manage comment placement, display, and editing; verify those interactions remain available.
The library load action now opens a general file picker but no longer passes the selected file to the previous library-import routine; verify that importing a library file still adds its items.
The editor’s previous URL-based library import flow, including its confirmation and URL cleanup, is removed; verify that existing library-import links still work.
The embeddable editor package now publicly exposes utilities for parsing and handling library links for integrating developers.
Editor setup now waits until the editor API is available, and scene actions, clipboard copying, and exports use that API; verify these example capabilities remain usable after initialization.
Pointer movement now displays the pointer’s x and y coordinates in the example instead of only logging pointer updates; library handling is also connected through the library API.
qaChecks: Verify that opening the hash-parameter link imports its library items into the existing collection, retains existing items, opens the library collection, and removes the import parameter from the URL.
Check that opening the legacy query-parameter link also imports its items and removes that parameter from the URL.

Verify importing the library file adds the new item, does not add a duplicate of the existing item, and retains the existing item.
Verify selecting the valid library JSON file adds its items to the library.
Check that opening the existing library-import link for the hosted library file adds its items to the library.
Verify opening a legacy query-string library-import link imports the Library and does not replace the drawing that was already open.
Check that a locally saved Library is available after a fresh editor load.
Confirm that after a second tab updates the saved Library, returning to the first tab makes the updated items available.
Verify importing the Library file retains the existing item, adds the file’s item, opens the Library, and leaves the editor usable when the import finishes.
Check that startup data containing a Library item merges with an existing item rather than replacing it.
Confirm that a URL containing a valid Library link in the fragment’s Library-add parameter, or in the legacy query parameter, does not automatically add the linked items when the editor starts.
Validate that a scene update containing a nonempty Library collection leaves the Library unchanged, while a dedicated Library update with default options replaces the existing items.
Verify that loading a valid Library file imports its Library items and opens the Library; this file type previously went through the drawing-update path.
Check that loading a valid drawing file updates the displayed Scene.
Confirm that the footer comment control enters comment placement, and that clicking an existing comment lets you edit it and drag its marker.
Ensure the example's initial rocket image remains available after its data loads.
Verify that moving the pointer over the canvas updates the displayed x and y coordinates to match the pointer data; before moving it, both values should show 0.
Check that the example’s reusable drawing items are handled as library content and can be used from the library.
Confirm that scene setup completes and the example’s reset, clipboard-copy, and export capabilities remain usable after the editor initializes.
uncertainty: The supplied changes contain no prior implementation for comparison, so the input that the old behavior handled differently cannot be established; these checks verify the evidenced current behavior.

The previous link handler restored the address to its prior URL after a hash-based Library import; the new handler delegates this behavior, so confirm that importing a Library still leaves the address in the expected state.

The old import helper and merge routine are removed, but no replacement implementation is supplied; it is unclear whether this workflow was relocated or removed, and no specific old-versus-new input difference can be established.
The file-import path no longer explicitly clears the loading state after success or failure, so the editor’s usable state after an import should be confirmed.

For the image and comment changes, the evidence shows editor-API substitutions but does not identify an input that behaved differently before and after; confirm the expected example behavior with the checks above.
The new public library-link utilities may be intended to replace the removed URL import flow, but the supplied evidence does not show that connection; URL-based imports may no longer work.
The previous hash-change listener was removed, but the supplied evidence does not establish what behavior it handled or whether it was intended to remain.

report.summary: The release changes how text is sized, positioned, wrapped, and aligned across the editor and exported drawings.
keyChanges: Text width is now measured with canvas text metrics and text height is estimated at 1.2 times the font size per line, replacing browser-rendered measurements; text bounds may therefore change during creation, editing, resizing, and restoration.
Line wrapping now treats a word whose width exactly matches the available width as a single fitting line, rather than breaking it across lines.
New text is no longer shifted upward by half its baseline when created outside a container, and newly created text no longer stores a baseline value; check its placement and chart text rendering.
Estimated line height now uses 1.2 times the font size instead of measured canvas height, and bound-text editing now sets the editor height from measured wrapped text even for a single line.
Text editing no longer caps editor width at the available maximum; Firefox and Safari add 0.5px to the text element width.

Text widths are now measured without the previous 0.2-pixel padding, and text dimension refresh no longer reapplies the container width constraint; text near a wrapping boundary may therefore lay out differently. Baseline recalculation was also removed from text refresh and bound-text redraw.
When a saved drawing restores text that contains a baseline value, that value is no longer explicitly copied into the restored text; verify the text still appears correctly.
When bound text is detached from its shape, its measured baseline is no longer explicitly assigned; verify the detached text remains correctly laid out.

Resizing text and bound text now calculates font size from width rather than both width and height, and no longer updates the text baseline during these resize paths; verify text remains readable and correctly laid out when resized.
When bound text is resized with its container, wrapping is followed by text measurement without an explicit maximum-width argument, so unusually long unbroken text is a useful edge case to check.

Canvas text is now drawn using a bottom baseline at each line-height position instead of offsets derived from the stored baseline and, for bottom-aligned bound text, a bound-text offset; SVG text positioning now uses the full text height instead of the stored baseline.
qaChecks: Verify text containing the exact-width word "TEST" in a container with available width equal to that word's rendered width stays together on one line.
Check pasted text containing a CRLF line break, such as "First line\r\nSecond line", displays as two lines and its text bounds match the displayed lines.
Confirm editing text with several lines and an empty line keeps the line breaks visible and the text positioned within its bounds.
Verify that creating new text on empty canvas places it without the former upward shift of half its baseline.

Check bound text in Firefox using one line of 16px handwritten-style text: the new estimated line height is 19.2px rather than the prior browser-measured value; confirm editing and deleting the line keeps the text positioned correctly without jumping.
Confirm that editing a single line of text bound to a shape sizes the editor from the measured text height, and that text remains readable and aligned.

Test editing a text element wider than the available viewport, especially in Firefox or Safari; confirm the editor remains aligned with the canvas text and check whether its uncapped width causes visible clipping or overflow.
Verify that the chart preview and inserted chart display the title and labels in the expected positions and remain readable.
Verify that entering the prepared text in the shape keeps it on one line; the previous 0.2-pixel padding would have made this input exceed the available width and wrap.
Check that editing the attached text still leaves it positioned within its shape, including when the text spans multiple lines.
Verify opening the saved drawing with a baseline value on its text keeps that text visible and correctly laid out.
Check that detaching the bound text from its shape leaves the text visible and correctly laid out.
Verify that after narrowing the shape, its bound text containing the long unbroken word remains readable and does not spill outside the shape.
Check that resizing the shape wider while its height remains short leaves the bound text legible and positioned with the shape.
Confirm that resizing the separate text item keeps its text legible and its visible position aligned with the item.
Verify that the two-line, bottom-aligned bound text appears in its intended position within the shape or connector when displayed on the canvas.
Verify that the SVG export keeps both text lines legible and in their intended position relative to the shape or connector.

report.summary: The release improves how users create and edit arrow connections on the drawing canvas.
keyChanges: Arrow hit-testing now accepts one shared numeric tolerance instead of a per-shape tolerance function, allowing elbow-arrow endpoint binding to use its numeric distance limit without treating it as a function.

When arrow reordering receives an already identified target, it uses that target rather than performing another pointer hit-test, which can affect which shape and attached text the arrow is layered above.
Arrow endpoint dragging now supplies a numeric binding-distance limit rather than a per-element distance callback, affecting how ordinary and elbow arrows find nearby shapes.
When repositioning one arrow endpoint, the check for whether the other endpoint’s focus point is inside its already-connected shape now uses shape hit detection with interior testing enabled.

Dragging an arrow endpoint can attach it to an eligible shape, detach it when moved off a target, and update the other bound endpoint; holding Alt switches the connection to inside mode, while releasing it returns to orbit mode.

When multiple shapes are candidates, endpoint targeting checks from front to back and chooses the first candidate that is inside the shape or within its binding gap; endpoint calculations now use the shape’s geometry-based center, and rectangular corners no longer use the previous corner-avoidance adjustment.

For bound, non-elbow arrows with exactly two points, focus-point indicators and interaction are available when binding is enabled and the focus point lies on the connected shape without overlapping the arrow endpoint.
Dragging an endpoint focus point to another shape and releasing updates which shape records the arrow connection.
Dragging an interior point of an arrow now recalculates its bound endpoints; previously, when neither endpoint was selected, their positions were left unchanged.
Endpoint binding updates are now conditional when one endpoint is dragged onto the shape bound to the other, so verify the opposite endpoint is not shifted or rebound unexpectedly.
When a selected arrow has visible bindings to shapes, the canvas now shows focus points and dashed connection lines for its bound ends, providing clearer binding feedback.
During a drag of a selected line or arrow point, the hovered-point highlight is suppressed; the selected arrow is also resolved from the full drawing when rendering its editing feedback.
For a visible focus point on a bound arrow, the canvas draws a dashed connector and a circular marker; the marker is purple when hovered and white otherwise, with the highlight shown on hover.
The indicator drawing accounts for canvas scroll and scales its marker, stroke, and dash lengths inversely with zoom. The indicator is omitted while its selected arrow point is being dragged.

When an arrow or line point is actively being dragged, Alt-key presses and releases now trigger point or focus-binding updates; previously these updates were not routed through those keyboard events, including when complex bindings were disabled.
Clicking an arrow focus point now starts a binding drag even without a preceding pointer-move event; movement updates the binding, and releasing ends the drag.
Hovering a selected, connected arrow’s start or end focus point now marks that point as hovered and changes the cursor to a pointer, helping identify the connection point.

report.summary: The release updates how drawing objects are selected and interacted with, how frames identify included content, and related editor settings.
keyChanges: Bounds containment now treats points on all four edges as inside, affecting selection and frame-content decisions for elements that touch a boundary.
Pointer hit-testing for rotated elements now follows their rotated bounds instead of the larger axis-aligned box, so clicks in the old box’s corner regions may no longer hit the element.
Free-drawn elements now use their absolute coordinates when calculating their center, which can affect arrow connections and snapping around those strokes.
Curved lines, arrows, and free-draw strokes can now use up to 10 solver iterations when checking intersections, instead of the previous 4, so some previously missed intersections may now be detected.
Hit testing now accounts for an element’s rotation by checking the pointer against its rotated bounds, which may change which points on rotated elements respond to clicks.

New drawings default to contain-mode box selection, and restoring a drawing now preserves its saved box-selection mode; the setting is included in browser state but excluded from exports and server state.
Frame exports now provide the full drawing’s element map when determining which elements overlap the exported frame, which may affect the exported contents.
Bounds calculations can now expand by an explicitly supplied padding amount on every side; the supplied application callers omit that option, so their bounds remain unchanged.
The production web build now preloads the Assistant semibold font, which should make that font available earlier during page loading.

Box selection now includes an object’s stroke and any text attached to an arrow when checking whether the selection box contains it, so a box that encloses the arrow but not its attached text no longer selects the arrow.
Selection logic also supports an overlap mode that can select objects when the box crosses their outline; the default remains contain mode.

Frame contents used by generation and frame-only exports are now determined by strict intersection of element and frame bounds, while elements assigned to a different frame remain excluded; bounds that only touch at an edge do not intersect.
Alt+Ctrl/Command now forces lasso selection even when starting on a selected element or the shared bounds of a selection, except when starting on a resize handle.

The shared hit area for multiple selected elements expands by twice the transform-handle spacing at the current zoom; hovering there without Ctrl/Command now shows the move cursor and can affect selection dragging and context-menu targeting.
Box-selection mode is now passed into selection calculation, so selection results may differ when that mode is active.
Framed-diagram generation now supplies the current non-deleted scene-element map when identifying frame contents. The evidence does not establish which inputs change the identified contents.
Preferences now offers contain and overlap box-selection modes, and radio-choice rows can show an icon and truncate overflowing titles; verify the new choice and its menu layout.
qaChecks: Verify a selection box whose edge exactly touches an element’s edge includes that boundary when using containment selection.
Check that an element whose edge exactly touches a frame’s edge is treated as fully within the frame.
Verify a click in an axis-aligned bounding-box corner outside the rotated rectangle does not hit the selected element, while a click on the visible rectangle still hits it.
Test connecting the arrow to the asymmetric freehand stroke and verify the connection and snapping align with the stroke.
Verify a curved free-draw stroke or arrow crossed by a lasso at a point that needs 5 to 10 solver iterations is selected where the paths cross.
Check that an eraser stroke crossing the same kind of curved stroke erases the crossed element.
Confirm an arrow endpoint can bind to a shape when dragged to its rotated outline.
Test clicking the visible body of a rotated shape and a point outside its rotated outline but inside its unrotated bounding box; the shape should respond to the first point, not the second.
Verify that after loading the drawing, a selection box selects elements fully enclosed by it and does not select elements that extend outside it.
Check that exporting the target frame includes its overlapping content and excludes the element assigned to the other frame.
Verify the Assistant semibold font is requested during initial loading and that semibold text renders in Assistant after the page loads.
Verify that a box enclosing the arrow but excluding its attached text does not select the arrow, and that expanding the box to contain both selects it.
Check that a box tracing a shape’s path but cutting off its outer stroke does not select the whole shape in the default contain mode.
Verify that, when overlap mode is requested, a selection box crossing an object’s outline can select that object.
Verify frame-only export and frame-based generation with the edge-touching element: it should not count as frame content; the element extending inside the frame should be included.
Verify Alt+Ctrl/Command-click-drag starting on a selected element away from resize handles starts lasso selection instead of simply dragging the selected element.

Check a point just outside the old shared-bounds hit area but within the added padding of 2 × transform-handle spacing ÷ zoom; without Ctrl/Command, confirm the move cursor appears and dragging moves the selected elements rather than starting a lasso.
Confirm that a selection box partially overlapping an element produces a result consistent with the active box-selection mode.
Test framed-diagram generation with a frame containing a non-deleted drawing element and confirm generation uses the frame's contents.
Verify the box-selection setting is present and selecting contain, then overlap, updates the selected radio to each chosen value.
Check a preference title longer than its available row width; it should remain on one line and end with an ellipsis.

The supplied evidence does not identify a reproducible curve-and-line placement that needs 5 to 10 solver iterations, and it does not show the previous rotated-bounds logic, so these checks target plausible regression edges rather than a confirmed specific failure.

report.summary: The release reshapes URL and query-string handling, changing how addresses are parsed, composed, and inspected.
keyChanges: Inputs without a protocol now take the path-parsing route, retaining query text as a search string instead of parsing it immediately into parameters.
Absolute URLs now retain credentials together and keep the host and port together rather than separating username, password, hostname, and port.
Query-string handling parses repeated nonempty keys into multiple values and serializes empty values as keys without an equals sign.
URL host parsing now supplies separate hostname and port values, so port-bearing hosts need verification.
The supplied query parsing and duplicate-key conversion code was removed; the evidence does not show how that behavior is replaced.
URL construction now uses the new URL representation, which parses string input and rejects non-string input; normalization and resolution also use it.
URL composition adds query values, joins non-empty path segments, replaces the hash when the appended URL has one, and rejects appended URLs that include a protocol.
String conversion returns the URL’s href, while its full path encodes the path and hash.
The exported URL-parameter reader has been removed, so consumers that relied on it can no longer import it.
New query utilities read query values and add supplied values to a URL; supplied values override existing values with the same key while other existing values are retained.
Protocol detection now recognizes only a word-character scheme before "://", so a scheme such as "web+demo://" is treated as a path rather than a protocol URL.
The package entry point now exposes query and URL modules and no longer re-exports the UFO module, changing which capabilities package consumers can access.

Query-string formatting emits a bare key for an empty or undefined value and repeats a key for each array value; URL wrapper string and JSON conversion methods were removed, affecting URL utility calls and serialization.
The former URL class and its methods are deleted; no replacement behavior is shown for parsing URL input, appending paths and parameters, or producing host and credential text.
URL credentials are split into a username and password and percent-decoded; the encoded credential form percent-encodes both values and omits the colon when the password is empty.
The query-string encoder was removed even though the URL search accessor calls it; empty values previously produced a bare parameter name, so URL search formatting needs focused verification.
URL objects now expose query parameters as URLSearchParams, preserving repeated values and representing a falsy single value as an empty value, and serialize to their href as JSON.
The previous helper merged supplied parameters into a URL, with supplied values overriding matching existing ones; no production callers or user-facing surfaces are identified.
The utility no longer provides the former accessors for a URL’s href, origin, authenticated origin, encoded query string, or URLSearchParams; previously, query arrays produced repeated parameters.
A protocol is considered present when its string is nonempty, and a URL is absolute when it has a protocol or its path starts with “/”.

Origin and full-address values include the encoded host; the full address adds the origin only when both a protocol and an absolute URL are present, while query text is empty for an empty query and otherwise starts with “?”.

report.summary: The release expands shared logging and interactive prompt capabilities across console and browser environments.
keyChanges: The shared package entry no longer exposes the logger-creation factory, so consumers importing it from that entry will need to use another supported entry point.
Selection prompts now define distinct displays for active, inactive, selected, and cancelled options; multiselect options also show hints, while grouped options include group-line markers.
Prompt status indicators are defined in cyan for initial or active, red for cancelled, yellow for errors, and green for submitted.
Confirmation prompts default to “Yes” selected, and show the chosen answer when submitted or cancelled.

Multi-selection requires at least one choice by default, while setting the requirement to false permits an empty selection; text prompts show their placeholder for an empty value, and single-choice prompts display the selected option.
Cancellation output prints the supplied message in red followed by two newline characters, or just the newlines when no message is supplied.
Creating a logger now applies the environment-appropriate default reporter when none is supplied and adds prompt support; explicitly supplied logger options are passed through.
Interactive prompts now support text, confirmation, single selection, and multiple selection, including string choices converted to selectable labels and values.
Messages are formatted with a gray divider; multiline messages put the status marker on the first line and a divider on each continuation line.
Info, error, step, and success messages now use blue, red, and green status markers respectively; warning messages also use the shared formatter.
Prompt and status symbols now select Unicode glyphs when supported and defined text fallbacks otherwise, affecting how terminal prompts and results appear.
Notices are printed in a framed layout whose width calculation ignores ANSI escape sequences, so colored text is measured by its visible characters.
The prompt capability now accepts prompt configuration and forwards requests to a configured handler; without one, it throws an unsupported-prompt error.

A new example asks for a name, confirmation, project type, and optional tools, demonstrating initial text, placeholders, choices, and hints. No application navigation or user-facing surface was supplied.

Browser logger creation now accepts options, keeps the browser reporter by default, and lets supplied options override defaults; an empty reporter list is preserved rather than replaced with the default.
The browser logger now handles confirmation prompts with a browser confirmation dialog and other prompts with a browser text-entry dialog, returning the result in a promise.

Grouped prompts run in key order and each receives results collected so far; when a prompt is canceled and an on-cancel handler is provided, its result is recorded as "canceled" and the handler receives the collected results.

Grouped multi-selection requires at least one choice by default, while explicitly setting required to false allows an empty selection; grouped options also display selection and prompt states in the terminal.
Introductions print a gray divider and title, while warning messages use a warning marker and the warning alias forwards to the same behavior.
Password prompts display masked input and render validation errors, submission, and cancellation states.
Key-selection prompts display available choices and identify the selected or cancelled choice.
Spinner messages remove one to three trailing periods while progress runs, and the completion message is displayed when it stops.
Completion messages are written between divider lines.
